findings.title: Crash when Google Meet is selected without a destination calendar
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is the first element of `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so it is undefined when the event has no destination calendar. The next condition dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. Previously optional chaining made this safe. Any Google Meet booking without a destination calendar now throws inside EventManager.create instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Stale credential reused when a reference credential cannot be loaded
findings.body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents` the loop reuses the outer `credential` variable. If `this.calendarCredentials` has no match and the DB lookup fails or returns a credential without `app.slug`, `credential` still holds the previous iteration's credential or remains undefined. The code then calls `updateEvent(credential, ...)`, potentially updating the wrong calendar or failing. It should skip that reference when no credential is resolved and scope the variable per iteration.

findings.title: Updated calendar references lose credentialId and externalCalendarId
findings.body: `referencesToCreate` for `updateLocation` now reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` never puts those fields on its returned EventResult. Editing a booking location therefore creates BookingReference rows with both fields undefined. Previously the `evt.destinationCalendar` fallback populated them. Later updates/cancellations may then target the wrong calendar or fail to find the external event.

findings.title: Collective hosts' destination calendars are dropped when the organizer has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is explicitly set to `null` when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination calendar. The optional push then silently does nothing, so `teamDestinationCalendars` collected from the other collective hosts is discarded. In that case EventManager never receives those hosts' destination calendars and collective hosts do not get calendar invites. The array should be initialised to `[]` before collecting/pushing team destinations.

findings.title: Organization slug creation is inverted for self-hosted billing settings
findings.body: This PR changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. When team billing is disabled, which is the normal self-hosted path, the organization is now created without a slug, whereas previously it always received one. This is unrelated to the destination-calendar fix and will break organization URLs on instances without team billing.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses undefined calendarId when destination is absent
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` can be undefined when no destination calendar matches the credential, and insert correctly falls back to `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. The follow-up `events.patch` still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, so in the fallback case the patch is sent with an undefined calendar id and the generated hangoutLink is not written into the event description. Use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` fallback in the patch.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback compares externalId with the null externalCalendarId
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is not provided, the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Because `externalCalendarId` is null/undefined, this almost always returns undefined. Previously it fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Updates may now fail because calendarId is undefined, and deletes fall back to `primary` instead of the event's destination calendar, leaving events behind. The same broken pattern exists in `deleteEvent` at line 317.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent writes to the first host's calendar for every credential
findings.body: `createEvent` ignores the new `credentialId` argument and always chooses `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId`. When EventManager iterates collective hosts, the second host's Office365 credential is used against the first host's calendar id, causing 403/404 errors or creating the event in the wrong calendar. It needs to select the destination whose `credentialId` matches the credential passed to `createEvent`.

findings.title: Lark createEvent also ignores credentialId and uses the first destination
findings.body: The Lark implementation now takes the first element of `event.destinationCalendar` for every credential. For a collective booking, the second host's Lark credential will attempt to use the first host's calendarId, likely failing or writing to the wrong calendar. `createEvent` needs to choose the destination entry matching the credential it was called with.

findings.title: Base CalDAV service ignores credentialId when selecting destination calendars
findings.body: With multiple destination calendars, `createEvent` filters the credential's calendars by the first destination's externalId. For the second host's credential that externalId belongs to another account, so the filter produces no calendars and the method returns success without creating anything. The selection must be made using the `credentialId` passed to `createEvent` or another identifier that belongs to the current credential.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancellation only uses organizer credentials and repeats deletes
findings.body: When cancelling all remaining recurring bookings, the loop over the new multiple calendar references re-enters the same block for every reference, but inside it ignores the current reference and only iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, deleting the first calendar reference of every updated booking. For a collective booking, second-host references/credentials are never used, so those external events remain, and the same organizer deletions are issued once per reference.

findings.title: No test for collective multi-host destination calendars
findings.body: The only test change updates the expected webhook shape for BOOKING_REJECTED. There is no test covering collective events with multiple destination calendars or the new create/update/delete paths, despite many calendar services and EventManager being changed. This leaves the primary regression and the calendar-service credential-selection bugs untested.
